sentences.en: From The New York Times, I'm Rachel Abrams, and this is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 来自《纽约时报》，我是雷切尔·艾布拉姆斯，这是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: For decades, breast augmentations have been one of the most popular cosmetic surgeries in America.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，隆胸手术一直是美国最受欢迎的整形手术之一。

sentences.en: But in recent years, a new trend has started to emerge.
sentences.zh: 但近年来，一股新趋势开始出现。

sentences.en: The Breast Reduction.
sentences.zh: 缩胸手术。

sentences.en: Today, my colleague Lisa Miller on understanding the appeal of the smaller breaSt.
sentences.zh: 今天，我的同事丽莎·米勒将带我们了解小胸的吸引力。

sentences.en: It's Wednesday, November 20th.
sentences.zh: 今天是11月20日，星期三。

sentences.en: Hi, Lisa.
sentences.zh: 嗨，丽莎。

sentences.en: Hi, Rachel.
sentences.zh: 嗨，雷切尔。

sentences.en: So, you recently wrote a story about something that I am pretty sure we haven't covered on the daily before.
sentences.zh: 所以，你最近写了一篇报道，关于一件我确信我们以前在《每日新闻》里没有涵盖过的事。

sentences.en: And that topic is breast reductions.
sentences.zh: 这个话题就是缩胸手术。

sentences.en: And I'd really love to hear, before we get into it, why you wrote about it and why it interested you.
sentences.zh: 在深入探讨之前，我真的很想听听你为什么写这个话题，以及它为什么吸引了你。

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: I work on the Well Desk at The New York Times.
sentences.zh: 我在《纽约时报》的“健康”专栏工作。

sentences.en: And Well is the area of The Times that covers health and wellness, nutrition, fitness.
sentences.zh: “健康”是《时报》涵盖健康与保健、营养、健身的领域。

sentences.en: I am particularly interested in the subject of women's bodies and how it feels to be in a female body walking around in the world.
sentences.zh: 我对女性身体的主题特别感兴趣，以及作为一个女性在世界上行走时，拥有女性身体的感受是什么样的。

sentences.en: So, those are the kinds of stories that I do.
sentences.zh: 所以，这些就是我所做的报道。

sentences.en: So, my colleague, Stella Bugbee, who is the editor of The Styles Desk, handed me these numbers one day.
sentences.zh: 有一天，我的同事斯特拉·巴格比，也就是“时尚”专栏的编辑，交给我这些数字。

sentences.en: And the numbers were from the American Society of Plastic Surgeons.
sentences.zh: 这些数字来自美国整形外科医生协会。

sentences.en: And they showed this dramatic increase in breast reductions over the last five years, driven by women under 30.
sentences.zh: 它们显示，在过去五年里，在30岁以下女性的推动下，缩胸手术出现了惊人的增长。

sentences.en: And she was just like, what do you think is going on here?
sentences.zh: 她当时就说，你觉得这里发生了什么？

sentences.en: So, I just set about sort of exploring both why the trend and also sort of what was in women's heads as they were making these decisions.
sentences.zh: 所以我开始着手探讨这个趋势的原因，以及女性在做出这些决定时的想法。

sentences.en: Can you tell us a little bit about those numbers specifically?
sentences.zh: 你能具体给我们讲讲这些数字吗？

sentences.en: What did they show and what were they?
sentences.zh: 它们显示了什么，具体数字是多少？

sentences.en: So, in 2023, which is the last year for which data are available, more than 76,000 women had breast reductions.
sentences.zh: 在2023年，即可获得数据的最后一年，有超过76,000名女性做了缩胸手术。

sentences.en: And these are not surgeries that have to do with cancer, and they're not gender-affirming surgeries.
sentences.zh: 这些不是与癌症相关的手术，也不是性别确认手术。

sentences.en: These are surgeries that insurance companies deem to be cosmetic.
sentences.zh: 这些是保险公司认为是整形的手术。

sentences.en: And it was just an astonishing jump from pre-pandemic when the number was more like 40,000.
sentences.zh: 与大流行前大约40,000人的数字相比，这是一个惊人的飞跃。

sentences.en: And, you know, to be sure, the most popular cosmetic breast surgery in the country is breast augmentation still.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，可以肯定的是，国内最受欢迎的隆胸手术仍然是隆胸。

sentences.en: These numbers are tiny in comparison to the numbers of women who are getting augmentations.
sentences.zh: 与做隆胸手术的女性人数相比，这些数字微不足道。

sentences.en: 300,000 about get an augmentation every year.
sentences.zh: 每年大约有30万人进行隆胸。

sentences.en: But those numbers are creeping downward.
sentences.zh: 但这些数字正在小幅下降。

sentences.en: And the reduction numbers are going upward, not just among young women, but among women in every age group.
sentences.zh: 而缩胸的数字正在上升，不仅在年轻女性中，而且在各个年龄段的女性中都是如此。

sentences.en: You know, it's funny.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这很有趣。

sentences.en: I feel like I, too, have noticed this trend towards smaller breasts in popular culture.
sentences.zh: 我觉得我似乎也注意到了流行文化中向小胸发展的这种趋势。

sentences.en: I can't really put my finger on it exactly, but I feel like I've walked into stores where you see dresses that you really can only wear if you have small breasts.
sentences.zh: 我真的说不准具体是什么，但我感觉我走进商店时看到的连衣裙，真的只有小胸才能穿。

sentences.en: It feels like there are more models with small breasts on the runway.
sentences.zh: 感觉T台上有更多小胸模特了。

sentences.en: And I've noticed this sort of anecdotally here and there, but I didn't realize at all that that trend was actually something quantifiable and showing up in data somewhere.
sentences.zh: 我零零星星地注意到了这一点，但我根本没意识到这种趋势实际上是可量化的，并且在某处的数里显示出来了。

sentences.en: Totally.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: I mean, I was thinking about this before I came to record this session, and I was like, it's a little bit like learning a new word, and then you hear that word everywhere.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，在我来录制这期节目之前，我一直在想这件事，我觉得这有点像学了一个新词，然后你到处都能听到这个词。

sentences.en: Yes, totally.
sentences.zh: 是的，完全是这样。

sentences.en: So, you know, I saw these numbers, and I was like, hmm.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，我看到了这些数字，然后我想，嗯。

sentences.en: And then I went out into the world, and like in Brooklyn where I live, so many young women are wearing like tank tops and camisoles without bras, slip dresses without bras.
sentences.zh: 然后我走到外面，就像在我居住的布鲁克林，很多年轻女性穿着不穿文胸的背心和吊带衫，不穿文胸的吊带裙。

sentences.en: In LA, where I went to report the story, I saw all these women wearing these smock dresses where you couldn't wear a bra.
sentences.zh: 在洛杉矶，我去那里做这篇报道，我看到所有这些女性都穿着那种无法穿文胸的罩衫裙。

sentences.en: As I'm well aware of the smock dress.
sentences.zh: 我对罩衫裙深有体会。

sentences.en: And so it just, it really did feel like it was everywhere all at once.
sentences.zh: 所以，这真的让人感觉它无处不在。

sentences.en: And also, I mean, it just sort of runs counter to, I think, a lot of the imagery that like we've grown up with in terms of what was on television.
sentences.zh: 而且，我的意思是，这与我们电视上从小看到的大多数意象背道而驰。

sentences.en: Like, there's a reason why breast augmentation surgeries got so big.
sentences.zh: 比如，隆胸手术之所以变得如此盛行是有原因的。

sentences.en: I mean, you know, when I was growing up, being flat-chested was a mortification.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你知道，自我成长的时候起，平胸是一种羞辱。

sentences.en: Nobody wanted to be flat-chested.
sentences.zh: 没有人想当平胸。

sentences.en: I remember this distinctly from high school.
sentences.zh: 我从高中起就对此记忆犹新。

sentences.en: Everybody admired the girls with bigger boobs.
sentences.zh: 每个人都羡慕胸部更大的女孩。

sentences.en: The big girls with bigger boobs, like, showed off in the locker room.
sentences.zh: 胸部更大的大女孩，在更衣室里炫耀。

sentences.en: This was the 80s.
sentences.zh: 那是80年代。

sentences.en: And, you know, that was the era of silicone breast implants.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，那是硅胶隆胸的时代。

sentences.en: That was the era of big-breasted models.
sentences.zh: 那是大胸模特的时代。

sentences.en: Dolly Parton.
sentences.zh: 多莉·帕顿。

sentences.en: Dolly Parton.
sentences.zh: 多莉·帕顿。

sentences.en: I'd be remiss if I didn't bring up Hooters, which I do not, I do not feel like you could have launched that now, but that is a big restaurant chain that launched, I think, in
sentences.zh: 如果我不提Hooters，那我就是失职了，我觉得你现在不可能推出那个了，但那是一家大型连锁餐厅，我想它是在

sentences.en: the 80s or 90s.
sentences.zh: 80年代或90年代推出的。

sentences.en: It was all okay.
sentences.zh: 这一切都很好。

sentences.en: And not only was it all okay, it was all desirable.
sentences.zh: 不仅一切都好，而且一切都令人向往。

sentences.en: I mean, as one of the women I spoke to for the story said to me, like, when you have big breasts, you're winning.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，正如我为这篇报道采访的一位女性对我说的那样，当你有大胸时，你就是赢家。

sentences.en: She's like, that's what culture thinks about big breasts.
sentences.zh: 她说，这就是文化对大胸的看法。

sentences.en: And when you go back, that goes back to post-World War II voluptuousness, right?
sentences.zh: 当你回溯时，这可以追溯到二战后的丰满感，对吧？

sentences.en: Like, Marilyn Monroe leads into Baywatch, leads into Kardashians.
sentences.zh: 就像玛丽莲·梦露接着是《海岸救生队》，接着是卡戴珊家族。

sentences.en: It's this kind of ostentatious display of femaleness.
sentences.zh: 这是一种对女性特质的炫耀性展示。

sentences.en: Big breasts meant power.
sentences.zh: 大胸意味着力量。

sentences.en: They meant sex.
sentences.zh: 它们意味着性感。

sentences.en: They meant motherhood.
sentences.zh: 它们意味着母性。

sentences.en: They were something that men wanted.
sentences.zh: 它们是男人想要的东西。

sentences.en: And if you had them, you know, it was money in the bank.
sentences.zh: 如果你拥有它们，你知道，那就是稳赚不赔。

sentences.en: And so, by the 2010s, breast augmentation, which had gotten more and more and more sophisticated,
sentences.zh: 因此，到了2010年代，变得越来越成熟的隆胸手术，

sentences.en: the implants had gotten more and more and more natural looking, was the most popular cosmetic surgery in the country.
sentences.zh: 假体变得越来越自然，成为了国内最受欢迎的整形手术。

sentences.en: 350,000 women a year were getting a breast augmentation.
sentences.zh: 每年有35万名女性接受隆胸手术。

sentences.en: Everything you're saying, I mean, all of our experiences, I think, add up to the idea that it's not groundbreaking to say that Americans have been pretty obsessed with the female
sentences.zh: 你所说的一切，我的意思是，我们所有的经历，我认为都归结为一个观点，即说美国人对女性

sentences.en: breast, right?
sentences.zh: 乳房相当痴迷，这并不是什么石破天惊的话，对吧？

sentences.en: No, not at all.
sentences.zh: 不，一点也不。

sentences.en: It's not groundbreaking.
sentences.zh: 这不是什么开创性的观点。

sentences.en: I mean, there's been this obsession with breasts in culture for, you know, ever.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，文化中对乳房的这种痴迷已经持续了，你知道，从古至今。

sentences.en: But what surprised me as I was doing the reporting was the extent to which this obsession not only extended into the medical community, but actually originated with it.
sentences.zh: 但让我在做报道时感到惊讶的是，这种痴迷不仅延伸到了医学界，而且实际上起源于医学界。

sentences.en: I had a conversation with a plastic surgeon who was a woman, and she was telling me about this paper that was published in 2011 in a plastic surgery journal in which an English
sentences.zh: 我和一位女性整形外科医生交谈过，她向我讲述了一篇在2011年发表在整形外科杂志上的论文，其中一位英国

sentences.en: plastic surgeon described the contours of the ideal breaSt.
sentences.zh: 整形外科医生描述了理想乳房的轮廓。

sentences.en: And the ideal breaSt.
sentences.zh: 以及理想的乳房。

sentences.en: The ideal breaSt.
sentences.zh: 理想的乳房。

sentences.en: Just one.
sentences.zh: 仅仅一个。

sentences.en: I mean, and he used that language in the paper, in this medical journal.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他在论文中使用了这种语言，在这本医学杂志中。

sentences.en: And this text became foundational.
sentences.zh: 这段文字成为了基础。

sentences.en: It became like a training text for generations of doctors.
sentences.zh: 它就像是一代又一代医生的培训教材。

sentences.en: And in the introduction to the paper, he talks about how, you know, Leonardo da Vinci defined the contours of the ideal human face.
sentences.zh: 在该论文的引言中，他谈到了列奥纳多·达·芬奇是如何定义理想人脸的轮廓的。

sentences.en: And he put this effort into that context.
sentences.zh: 他把这种努力放在了那个语境中。

sentences.en: Like, he was helping the profession of plastic surgeons create and improve breasts for the world.
sentences.zh: 就像，他是在帮助整形外科医生这个行业为世界创造和改善乳房。

sentences.en: He had this idea that the ideal breast was sort of concave below the nipple and sort of flat above the nipple.
sentences.zh: 他有一种观点，即理想的乳房在乳头下方呈凹形，在乳头上方呈平形。

sentences.en: So he was very specific in the shape of the ideal breaSt.
sentences.zh: 所以他对理想乳房的形状非常具体。

sentences.en: But no one has breasts like this.
sentences.zh: 但没有人有这样的乳房。

sentences.en: No one has breasts like this.
sentences.zh: 没有人有这样的乳房。

sentences.en: And yet the conventions around what a breast should look like are so strong and so established
sentences.zh: 然而，关于乳房应该长什么样的传统是如此强烈和根深蒂固，

sentences.en: that when a woman walks into a plastic surgeon's office, and remember, you know, four-fifths
sentences.zh: 以至于当一个女性走进整形外科医生的办公室时，记住，你知道，五分之四

sentences.en: of them are men, she says, I want something smaller, they say, well, your husband might not like that, or you should try losing some weight first, or I like them rounder.
sentences.zh: 的医生是男性，她说，我想要小一点的，他们会说，嗯，你丈夫可能不喜欢那样，或者你应该先减减肥，或者我喜欢更圆润的。

sentences.en: And there's a whole Reddit thread where women tell these stories to each other about walking into plastic surgeons' offices and asking for smaller breasts and the feedback they
sentences.zh: 有一个完整的Reddit帖子，女性在上面互相讲述她们走进整形外科医生办公室要求缩胸以及她们得到的

sentences.en: get.
sentences.zh: 反馈的故事。

sentences.en: It makes them feel like what they're asking for is crazy.
sentences.zh: 这让她们觉得自己要求的东西很疯狂。

sentences.en: So, obviously, Lisa, breast reduction sounds like a very self-evident term.
sentences.zh: 所以，很显然，丽莎，缩胸手术听起来是一个不言自明的词。

sentences.en: But just for the sake of it, can you walk us through what the surgery actually entails?
sentences.zh: 但为了以防万一，你能给我们讲讲这个手术究竟包含什么吗？

sentences.en: Yes, sure.
sentences.zh: 是的，当然。

sentences.en: So, the surgery usually involves, you know, making an incision around the nipple and then
sentences.zh: 所以，手术通常包括，你知道，在乳头周围做一个切口，然后

sentences.en: from the nipple down the length of the breast, the curved part of the breast, and then removing
sentences.zh: 从乳头顺着乳房的长度向下，也就是乳房的弯曲部分，然后切除

sentences.en: a lot of breast tissue from inside the breaSt.
sentences.zh: 乳房内部的大量乳房组织。

sentences.en: A thing that's really important to say here is that most of the women who go in for breast reduction have double D cups or bigger.
sentences.zh: 这里有一件非常重要的事情要说，那就是大多数去做缩胸手术的女性都拥有双D罩杯或更大。

sentences.en: And these days, the plastic surgeons told me, most women are asking for a B cup, whereas five years ago, they were wanting a C cup.
sentences.zh: 如今，整形外科医生告诉我，大多数女性要求B罩杯，而五年前，她们想要C罩杯。

sentences.en: So, they're asking for more breast tissue to be removed.
sentences.zh: 因此，她们要求切除更多的乳房组织。

sentences.en: And, you know, Kelly Killeen, who was one of the surgeons I spoke to for my story, I was talking to her in her office.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，凯利·基伦，我为我的报道采访过的外科医生之一，我在她的办公室里和她交谈。

sentences.en: She was wearing her scrubs.
sentences.zh: 她穿着手术服。

sentences.en: And I was like, but how much breast tissue are we talking about, actually?
sentences.zh: 然后我说，但是我们实际上在谈论多少乳房组织？

sentences.en: And she reached down and picked a Coke can up out of her garbage can.
sentences.zh: 她伸出手，从垃圾桶里拿出一个可口可乐罐。

sentences.en: And she was like, I just took this much breast tissue out of one breast in a patient.
sentences.zh: 她说，我刚刚从一个病人的一个乳房里取出了这么多的乳房组织。

sentences.en: Oh, my God.
sentences.zh: 哦，天哪。

sentences.en: You know, it's a lot.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这很多。

sentences.en: And so, it's a much more invasive surgery than augmentation.
sentences.zh: 所以，这是一种比隆胸侵入性大得多的手术。

sentences.en: And it has all of these potential consequences that are enduring.
sentences.zh: 它具有所有这些持久的潜在后果。

sentences.en: It can affect a woman's ability to breastfeed.
sentences.zh: 它会影响女性的母乳喂养能力。

sentences.en: There are not great data on this, but the best study says about a third of the time.
sentences.zh: 这方面没有很好的数据，但最好的研究表明大约有三分之一的几率。

sentences.en: It can affect nipple sensation.
sentences.zh: 它会影响乳头的敏感度。

sentences.en: And there's permanent scars that frequently go around the nipple, down the breast, under the breaSt.
sentences.zh: 并且会有永久性的疤痕，通常围绕着乳头，顺着乳房向下，直到乳房下方。

sentences.en: And the women are really making a big trade.
sentences.zh: 女性确实在做一笔巨大的交易。

sentences.en: You know, they're saying, I'm willing to do all of these things in order for my breasts to be smaller.
sentences.zh: 你知道，她们在说，为了让我的胸部变小，我愿意做所有这些事情。

sentences.en: And so, when they decide to make, as you said, that big trade and get the surgery anyway, what does it end up costing them?
sentences.zh: 所以，当她们决定进行你所说的那笔大交易并无论如何都要做手术时，这最终要花费她们多少钱？

sentences.en: The American Society of Plastic Surgeons says it costs about between $7,000 and $8,000.

sentences.zh: 站起来，去爱你自己所有的身形。

sentences.en: And so, you know, when I approached the Gen Z women and I was like, why do you want to do this, stipulating that, you know, there's pain and health concerns here.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，当我接近那些 Z 世代女性并问她们为什么想这样做时，在设定了这里存在疼痛和健康隐患的前提下。

sentences.en: However, what I was probing for, what I was poking at is, like, don't you think you're perfect already?
sentences.zh: 然而，我当时探究、追问的是，难道你们不觉得自己已经很完美了吗？

sentences.en: Why do you want to change your body?
sentences.zh: 为什么你们想改变自己的身体？

sentences.en: And what they said was surprising, which was like, no, no, I am doing this for me.
sentences.zh: 而她们的回答令人惊讶，她们说，不，不，我这么做是为了我自己。

sentences.en: This is autonomy.
sentences.zh: 这就是自主权。

sentences.en: And if I want a different kind of breast in order to wear a different kind of outfit or present in a different kind of way, that's not an admission that I'm capitulating.
sentences.zh: 如果我想要一种不同形态的胸部以便穿不同风格的衣服或以不同的方式展现自我，那并不承认我在妥协。

sentences.en: That's an expression of autonomy and independence and freedom, liberation.
sentences.zh: 那是自主权、独立和自由、解放的表达。

sentences.en: I just can't help but think, like, as you're talking about this, that this feels both new because we're talking about a trend of breast reductions, which is a new thing,
sentences.zh: 当你在谈论这个时，我禁不住在想，这既让人感觉新鲜，因为我们谈论的是一种缩胸的潮流，这是一件新鲜事，

sentences.en: but it also feels like kind of an age-old argument.
sentences.zh: 但这同时也让人感觉像是一个老生常谈的话题。

sentences.en: As long as plastic surgery has been around, it's been this debate of, like, are you doing it for you?
sentences.zh: 自从整容手术出现以来，就一直存在这样一场辩论：你是为了自己才做的吗？

sentences.en: Is it truly empowering?
sentences.zh: 这真的能赋予女性力量吗？

sentences.en: And even if you think it's truly empowering and you're doing it for you, you're actually doing it for somebody else.
sentences.zh: 而且，即使你认为这真的赋予了你力量，并且你是为了自己而做，但实际上你还是为了别人才做的。

sentences.en: And what do we think the right answer is for, like, who's allowed to do what?
sentences.zh: 对于“谁被允许做什么”，我们认为正确的答案是什么？

sentences.en: But even if a woman says that she's doing it for one reason, we can't always trust her that she understands her reason.
sentences.zh: 但即使一个女性说她这样做是出于某种原因，我们也不能总是相信她真正理解自己的动机。

sentences.en: So it feels like what's old is new again, I guess, a little bit.
sentences.zh: 所以感觉就像是旧瓶装新酒，我觉得，多少有一点。

sentences.en: I completely agree with you, and I thought about that a lot as I was reporting the story.
sentences.zh: 我完全同意你的看法，我在做这篇报道时也经常思考这个问题。

sentences.en: Like, why am I second-guessing the reasons that they're telling me?
sentences.zh: 比如，我为什么要质疑他们告诉我的那些理由呢？

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 是的，完全正确。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: And one of the most revelatory conversations I had was a conversation I had with a plus-size model who sort of confessed that she was considering a breast reduction.
sentences.zh: 我进行的最具启发性的对话之一，是与一位大码模特的谈话，她坦言自己正在考虑做缩胸手术。

sentences.en: And, you know, she makes her living being a person in a different body than the conventional ideal.
sentences.zh: 而且你知道的，她作为一个身材不同于传统审美标准的公众人物来谋生。

sentences.en: And yet she, too, was attracted by this idea that she might be able to unencumber herself by reducing her breasts.
sentences.zh: 然而，她也被这样一个想法吸引：通过缩胸，她或许能够让自己卸下负担。

sentences.en: I presented this dilemma to her, like, aren't you supposed to just love who you are?
sentences.zh: 我把这个困境抛给了她：难道你不是应该爱本来的自己吗？

sentences.en: She was like, yes, yes.
sentences.zh: 她说，是的，是的。

sentences.en: But we all live in the world.
sentences.zh: 但我们都生活在这个世界上。

sentences.en: We all take our bodies out into the world, and we get catcalled, and we get looked at, and we get judged, and people think things about us.
sentences.zh: 我们都把自己的身体带到这个世界上，我们会遭到吹口哨调戏，会被人打量，会被人评判，人们会对我们指指点点。

sentences.en: And it is impossible to be a female person in the world and not absorb those signals.
sentences.zh: 作为一个女性活在这个世界上，要做到不受这些信号的影响是不可能的。

sentences.en: And so, although in some ideal universe, we're able to live in our, you know, God-given bodies with happiness and ease, in the real world, that is impossible.
sentences.zh: 因此，尽管在某种理想的宇宙中，我们能够快乐而轻松地住在我们那，你知道的，上天赋予的身体里，但在现实世界中，这是不可能的。

sentences.en: So, given all of this, where did you actually land, you, yourself, as the reporter, who happens to be a person in the world,
sentences.zh: 所以，鉴于这一切，作为一名恰好也身处这个世界的记者，你本人最终得出了什么结论？

sentences.en: on this question of who is this for and whether this is just yet another way to make women feel inadequate about our bodies?
sentences.zh: 对于这究竟是为了谁，以及这是否只是又一种让女性对自己的身材感到不够完美的手段，你是怎么看的？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yes to both.
sentences.zh: 两者皆是。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Plus one.
sentences.zh: 同上。

sentences.en: Like, I think that the minute you try to make women choose, you're missing the point.
sentences.zh: 我觉得，只要你试图让女性去做选择，你就没有抓住重点。

sentences.en: And I see this in my own life, right?
sentences.zh: 我在自己的生活中也看到了这一点，对吧？

sentences.en: Like, I have a daughter, and I made sure always to tell her how beautiful she is, no matter what.
sentences.zh: 比如，我有一个女儿，我总是确保告诉她她是多么美丽，无论如何都是如此。

sentences.en: And I want her to grow up with a sense that, like, nothing about her body is a thing to be ashamed of or corrected or fixed or inadequate.
sentences.zh: 我希望她长大后有一种信念：她的身体没有任何值得羞愧、纠正、修复或感到不足的地方。

sentences.en: Like, that is the identity I hope that she carries through the world.
sentences.zh: 这就是我希望她带着走过世界的身份认同。

sentences.en: At the same time, I had breast cancer several years ago, and I had a breast reconstruction.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，我几年前得了乳腺癌，我做过乳房重建手术。

sentences.en: And so, as I think I alluded to, like, I am not a plastic surgery person.
sentences.zh: 所以，正如我刚才所暗示的，我并不是那种热衷于整容的人。

sentences.en: That is not my natural choice.
sentences.zh: 那不是我的自然选择。

sentences.en: And yet, the breast cancer forced me to have a breast reconstruction.
sentences.zh: 然而，乳腺癌迫使我进行了乳房重建。

sentences.en: And what I will say about that is that my breasts look better.
sentences.zh: 关于这一点，我想说的是，我的乳房看起来更好了。

sentences.en: They just do.
sentences.zh: 事实就是如此。

sentences.en: They just do.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: I'm, you know, a middle-aged, late middle-aged woman.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我是一个中年、快到中年的女性。

sentences.en: They had some miles on them.
sentences.zh: 我的身体已经经历了不少风雨。

sentences.en: I breastfed my daughter.
sentences.zh: 我用母乳喂养过我的女儿。

sentences.en: I ran two marathons.
sentences.zh: 我跑过两场马拉松。

sentences.en: Like, the lifted breast is, like, nice.
sentences.zh: 所以，挺拔起来的乳房确实挺好看的。

sentences.en: And so, although I wouldn't have chosen it, and I formerly would have had all kinds of judgment about it,
sentences.zh: 因此，尽管我本来不会选择它，而且我以前会对它抱有各种各样的评判，

sentences.en: I feel that it is an enhancement.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这是一种提升。

sentences.en: So, who am I to judge?
sentences.zh: 所以，我又有什么资格去评判别人呢？

sentences.en: Well, Lisa, it's been a pleasure.
sentences.zh: 好的，丽莎，很高兴能与你交流。

sentences.en: Thank you so much.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢。

sentences.en: It's been a pleasure.
sentences.zh: 我也很高兴。

sentences.en: Love being here.
sentences.zh: 很高兴能来到这里。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还需要了解的其他消息。

sentences.en: President-elect Trump continued a series of surprising choices for top roles in his second administration,
sentences.zh: 当选总统特朗普在他的第二任期内继续为高级职务物色一系列令人惊讶的人选，

sentences.en: picking celebrity physician Dr. Mehmet Oz to oversee the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services,
sentences.zh: 他挑选了名人医生、医学博士麦克姆·奥兹来监管联邦医疗保险和联邦医疗补助服务中心，

sentences.en: and Howard Lutnick, a Wall Street executive who's leading Trump's transition team, to serve as commerce secretary.
sentences.zh: 并挑选了领导特朗普过渡团队的华尔街高管霍华德·卢特尼克担任商务部长。

sentences.en: Lutnick, the head of financial firm Cantor Fitzgerald, would be in charge of an agency with an $11 billion budget and wide influence over broad swaths of the economy.
sentences.zh: 卢特尼克作为金融公司坎托·菲茨杰拉德的负责人，将掌管一个拥有110亿美元预算并在经济广泛领域具有巨大影响力的机构。

sentences.en: The choice of Dr. Oz, who's faced criticism for his sometimes dubious medical advice, comes after Trump chose Robert F.
sentences.zh: 挑选奥兹医生的决定是在特朗普选择小罗伯特·F·肯尼迪——一位知名的疫苗怀疑论者——领导卫生与公众服务部之后做出的，此前奥兹曾因其有时靠不住的医疗建议而面临批评。

sentences.en: Kennedy Jr., a notable vaccine skeptic, to lead the Department of Health and Human Services.
sentences.zh: 小罗伯特·F·肯尼迪是一名知名的疫苗怀疑论者，此前已被选为卫生与公众服务部负责人。

sentences.en: In his announcement, Trump said that the two men would work together to, quote, take on the illness industrial complex.
sentences.zh: 在宣布这一消息时，特朗普表示，这两名男子将共同致力于，引述，向疾病工业复合体发起挑战。

sentences.en: Today's episode was produced by Olivia Natt, Eric Krupke, and Rochelle Bonja.
sentences.zh: 今天的节目由奥利维亚·纳特、埃里克·克鲁普克和罗谢尔·邦贾制作。

sentences.en: It was edited by Mark George with help from Chris Haxel, contains original music by Leah Shaw Dameron, Alicia Baetup, and Marion Lozano, and was engineered by Alyssa Moxley.
sentences.zh: 由马克·乔治剪辑，克里斯·哈克尔提供协助，包含利亚·肖·达梅伦、艾莉西亚·拜图普和马里恩·洛扎诺创作的原声音乐，并由阿莉莎·莫克斯利进行音频工程处理。

sentences.en: Our theme music is by Jim Brunberg and Ben Landsberg of Wonderly.
sentences.zh: 我们的主题音乐由旺德利的吉姆·布伦伯格和本·兰斯伯格创作。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这就是本期《每日新闻》的内容。

sentences.en: I'm Rachel AbraMs.
sentences.zh: 我是雷切尔·亚伯拉罕斯。

sentences.en: See you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 明天见。

sentences.en: For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine,
sentences.zh: 几十年来，布鲁克林民主党一直作为一个受严密控制的机器在运作，

sentences.en: until this summer, when elections ushered in a bunch of self-described reformers.
sentences.zh: 直到今年夏天，选举迎来了大批自称改革派的人士。

sentences.en: Ever since, the party has been in the grip of a bruising, chaotic, and sometimes thrilling fight.
sentences.zh: 从那以后，该党一直陷入一场残酷、混乱且有时令人兴奋的权力斗争中。

sentences.en: In the latest episode of Metro, with me, Sarah Koenig, stories of people trying to maintain their influence and losing control along the way.
sentences.zh: 在由我莎拉·科尼格主持的最新一期《都市》节目中，我们将讲述人们试图维持自身影响力却在过程中失控的故事。

sentences.en: Metro.
sentences.zh: 《都市》。

sentences.en: Listen wherever you get your podcasts.
sentences.zh: 请在你获取播客的任何地方收听。
